uncertainties.note: Speaker of the rhetorical question ('Is a thing like that truly necessary for the world you want?') is not settled by the immediate context; could be a subordinate questioning Dewey's order to fire Oratorio No. 8, or Dewey's own rhetorical aside. Translated without assigning a specific speaker.
Line uses masculine 'boku' pronoun distinct from the adjacent 'ore' lines (Renton) and 'watashi' (Eureka); speaker not identified by name in this slice, so no character identity assigned.
'that girl' and 'that rider' both plausibly refer to Eureka, relayed secondhand by another crew member quoting the Nirvash; kept literal rather than collapsing into a single referent.
Short gasp/reaction syllable with no clear speaker tag; rendered as a neutral reaction ('...Huh?') rather than assigning identity.

Speaker resolved as Anemone from the following row (dialogue_10525) directly addressing 'Anemone' by name; 'that person' she says is nowhere to be found is not identified further (left as 'that person', no gender/name supplied).

Poetic first-person monologue (likely Eureka) that reads like it may echo an anime insert song's imagery; translated independently from the Japanese meaning in original wording, not copied from any existing English lyric translation.
'Ultimate' (katakana loanword, source: arutimetto) kept capitalized as a named power-output level for Oratorio No. 8; no existing glossary entry found for this specific usage. See glossary proposal.

validation.controls: All angle-bracket commands (<op()>/<on()>, <sp(20)>, <ab(n)>, <ed()>/<off()>) preserved in the source's exact order for every row, including rows where the source omits <op()>/<on()> or <ed()> because the text box stays open across adjacent rows (e.g. dialogue_10459-10461, dialogue_10475-10476, dialogue_10479-10483, dialogue_10520-10521, dialogue_10522-10524, dialogue_10526-10527, dialogue_10528-10529, dialogue_10534-10536). Verified with a throwaway self-check script comparing each row's command list against tools/dialogue_corpus.py slice output; no Japanese source text was written to disk.
validation.fit: Full meaning drafted first; longest visible rows recompressed to stay <=110 characters (e.g. dialogue_10533 combat-relay style compressed to 86 visible characters); all rows in slice at or under budget.
validation.ascii: ASCII-only; no lowercase j/q required by any row in this slice; no bare % encountered.
validation.meaning_review: Independently meaning-reviewed: 80 of 80 rows examined against original ISO with 30 rows of surrounding context (10442-10551). Three fixes applied (dialogue_10527 gender fix; dialogue_10487, dialogue_10524 reworded to drop an unnecessary lowercase j). All rows set to meaning_reviewed. See review_10457.json.
